fix_commits.message: Limit the number of channels a single transport process can join

severity.numeric_level_rationale: The EEF CNA, NVD and OSV all publish CVSS 4.0 8.7 High with the same vector. NVD additionally publishes a CVSS 3.1 7.5 High vector from nvd@nist.gov; the two differ only in metric version, not in the HIGH band.
severity.source: EEF CNA and NVD (CVSS 4.0 8.7); NVD also carries a CVSS 3.1 7.5 record

vulnerability.category_l2: Resource exhaustion: one transport process can join an unbounded number of channels because no per-transport channel cap is enforced

critical_operation.code_excerpt:
defp handle_in(nil, %{event: "phx_join", topic: topic, ref: ref, join_ref: join_ref} = message, state, socket) do
    case socket.handler.__channel__(topic) do
      {channel, opts} ->
        case Phoenix.Channel.Server.join(socket, channel, message, opts) do
          {:ok, reply, pid} ->
            reply = %Reply{join_ref: join_ref, ref: ref, topic: topic, status: :ok, payload: reply}
            state = put_channel(state, pid, topic, join_ref)
critical_operation.description: Each transport process (WebSocket or LongPoll) runs Phoenix.Socket.handle_in/4. The phx_join clause (595-613) resolves socket.handler.__channel__(topic) and, when a channel module is returned, calls Phoenix.Channel.Server.join/4 (line 598) and records the returned pid in state.channels via put_channel/4; the state created in user_connect/6 (line 544) contains only channels and channels_inverse, with no count, no per-transport ceiling and no rate limit. A client can therefore send phx_join messages for many acceptable topics over one connection and each accepted join leaves a persistent channel process, so a single unauthenticated transport can allocate processes without bound and exhaust the node. Persistence requires the resolved channel's join/3 to accept the topic (a wildcard channel such as room:* qualifies); joins the channel rejects do not leave a persistent process. The 1.6.17 fix adds max_channels_per_transport (default 100) to the transport state and rejects further joins with status :error once map_size(state.channels) reaches the limit (CWE-770).

entry_point.description: A remote client connects to a mounted Phoenix socket transport and sends repeated phx_join messages on the same WebSocket or LongPoll connection.

source_crosscheck.notes: CVE record, NVD and OSV agree on CWE-770, the 1.6.13-affected range and the 1.6.17 fix, and publish severity in two metric versions (CVSS 4.0 8.7 High and CVSS 3.1 7.5 High), both HIGH. The published lower bound disagrees: the CNA range starts at 0.11.0, while the NVD/OSV CPE-derived range starts at 1.2.0. Local inspection supports 0.11.0: v0.11.0 already keeps an uncapped per-transport sockets/sockets_inverse map and starts a Phoenix.Channel.Server for every phx_join. The OSV commit list mislabels the introducing commit 14a297e8 as fixed; ancestry maps the real fixes c498ba8c->1.5.15, d19ca0a8->1.6.17, a612100c->1.7.24, 16e295d2->1.8.9.

required_before_promotion: An independent reviewer must read handle_in/4 at v1.6.13 and confirm that phx_join has no per-transport cap and that each join creates a persistent channel process.
An independent reviewer must confirm d19ca0a8 is the 1.6-branch fix, not an ancestor of 1.6.13/1.6.16 and contained in 1.6.17.
An independent reviewer must confirm the affected ranges and the CVSS 4.0 / 3.1 records.
No formal reviews.jsonl row may be written until a named independent reviewer returns a verdict.
independent_corrections_accepted: 1.6 range upper bound is open at <1.6.17; the CNA's lower bound is 1.6.0-rc.0, so the 1.7/1.8 ranges were also corrected to their -rc.0 starts.

Lower bound: the CNA says 0.11.0 while NVD/OSV CPE ranges say 1.2.0; local inspection of v0.11.0 (uncapped sockets map, Channel.Server per phx_join) supports 0.11.0, so the 1.5-and-earlier range now starts at 0.11.0 with both claims recorded.
Impact narrowed: an accepted phx_join only leaves a persistent process when the resolved channel's join/3 accepts the topic (for example a wildcard room:* channel); rejected joins do not.
The vulnerable clause spans lines 595-613, while the verified location line remains 595-598 as returned by the independent reviewer.
Fix-commit mapping corrected after ancestry re-run: c498ba8c->1.5.15, a612100c->1.7.24, 16e295d2->1.8.9, and 14a297e8 is the introducing commit mislabeled as fixed by OSV.

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No Phoenix node, WebSocket client or process-exhaustion measurement was executed; the unbounded allocation is established statically.

Impact depends on the application mounting a socket transport reachable by the attacker and on a channel whose join/3 accepts attacker-chosen topics; the default Phoenix endpoint mounts a transport, but this dossier does not audit every deployment or channel.
Only the 1.6 branch was diffed; the 1.5.15, 1.7.24 and 1.8.9 fixed trees were not inspected.

The published lower bound is inconsistent (CNA 0.11.0, NVD/OSV CPE 1.2.0); 0.11.0 is used because v0.11.0 already contains the uncapped per-transport process bookkeeping, but the 0.11.x-1.1.x trees were not individually diffed.
OSV lists the introducing commit 14a297e8 as fixed; that is an upstream metadata defect, and the branch fixes are mapped by local ancestry instead.
open_questions: Whether transports apply any other per-connection message or process limit outside Socket.handle_in/4 was not exhaustively audited.
